title: Why do we have day and night?
summary: Earth spins once about every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun has daylight; the half turned away has night.
detail: Earth’s rotation makes the Sun appear to move across the sky. The seasons are a separate effect, caused mainly by Earth’s tilted axis as it travels around the Sun.
question: What causes the cycle of day and night?
answers: Earth moving farther from the Sun

title: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
summary: The Moon turns at the same rate it orbits Earth, keeping nearly the same face pointed our way.
detail: This synchronisation is called tidal locking. The Moon has a far side, but it is not permanently dark.
question: Does the Moon rotate on its axis?

title: What keeps planets in orbit?
summary: Gravity pulls planets toward the Sun while their forward motion carries them onward, producing curved paths called orbits.
detail: Every object with mass attracts other objects. The Sun contains most of the Solar System’s mass, so its gravity strongly shapes planetary motion.
question: What primarily keeps planets moving around the Sun?

title: How do stars shine?
summary: Stars shine because nuclear fusion in their cores releases energy that travels outward as light and heat.
detail: In a star like the Sun, hydrogen nuclei combine to form helium. This process releases energy over very long timescales.
question: What process powers a star like the Sun?

title: What is a galaxy?
summary: A galaxy is a vast collection of stars, gas, dust and dark matter held together by gravity.
detail: Our Solar System belongs to the Milky Way. Galaxies come in many shapes and can contain billions of stars.
question: What holds a galaxy together?

title: How do space telescopes help us explore?
summary: Space telescopes observe light beyond much of Earth’s atmosphere, helping scientists study distant objects and events.
detail: Different instruments observe different parts of the electromagnetic spectrum, from radio waves to gamma rays.
question: Why place some telescopes in space?
answers: To observe above much of Earth’s atmosphere
